commits.subject: Derive finite initialization strip walls and exact horizontal reset alternatives

modules.module_doc:
# A finite initialization strip around Start in a periodic horizontal row

The two first departures from the respective initializer tails must be
seams. Horizontal periodicity supplies finite departure witnesses using
Start on the left and the head initializer on the right. No unique Start,
time evolution, machine run, or rectangular tiling premise is used.

# Exact horizontal reset color in the actual finite tile language

A horizontal color 1 belongs only to a reset tile or an explicit seam
tile. The seam exception is retained in both directions. These are local
finite-table statements, not a claim that any whole row is a reset row.

Checks of every reset alternative and indispensable seam exceptions.
No propagation to a whole row, computation, or halting is asserted.

commits.subject: Derive fixed strip walls and a seam-free interior through all integer times

modules.module_doc:
# Fixed finite strip walls and a seam-free interior

The initial row determines the two walls and every interior tile. Actual
vertical matching preserves the wall columns and excludes seams at every
interior integer coordinate and time. No machine-run premise is used.

commits.subject: Bind the actual first machine step and exact configuration color semantics

modules.module_doc:
# The actual decimal machine's first blank-tape step

The authenticated action-cache theorem supplies the first decoded action;
the large decimal numeral is not reevaluated here. The resulting concrete
configuration writes a one at zero and moves right into state one. This is
the configuration represented by the initialization boundary components,
not the all-blank configuration before the first machine transition.
No tiling, machine-run extraction or consistency equivalence is assumed.

Exact first-step, integer tape, clock-shift and boundary-component checks.
No tiling premise and no second evaluation of the decimal numeral occur.

# Literal vertical colors of an actual machine configuration

Plain tape cells carry 0 or 1. The unique head carries `2*q+b+2`,
where operating states have q < 215 and the halted state has q = 215.
An action entering halt still writes and moves before this encoding is
applied; its final head has color 432 or 433 at the moved position.
This module defines no tiling or machine-run correspondence premise.

Checks for literal head-state colors, entering-halt write/move semantics,
and the exact actual initialization boundary. No tiling hypotheses occur.

commits.subject: Decode exact tile inputs and derive uniform finish rows from one event

modules.module_doc:
# Exact local input grammar of the actual 942 Wang tiles

An operating head input selects exactly its indexed transition. Halt
inputs admit pass and finish, and plain inputs admit pass, finish, or a
receive tile with an actual directional target. These are finite-language
statements, not machine-step or unique-head semantics for a whole row.

Checks of exact input indices, the actual halt transition, and all
nondeterministic local plain/halt alternatives that must remain present.

# Propagating one actual reset across a seam-free integer interval

Color1 propagates in both horizontal directions. The exact local tile
classification then forces a reset at each interior position. The only
geometry input is explicit absence of seams in that interval; periodicity,
unique Start, an assumed reset row and machine semantics are not used.

Focused checks: arbitrary signed intervals, singleton interiors,
all local reset/finish variants, indispensable seam exclusion, and the
actual marked-plane geometry supplied without a uniform-row premise.

commits.subject: Identify the actual clock1 row and rule out premature finishes in operating rows

modules.module_doc:
# An operating encoded row cannot finish anywhere inside its strip

The unique head input forces its actual transition tile. A finish at any
interior position would force finish at the head through the next reset
row, contradicting the transition's Boolean South output. Absence of
finishes is a conclusion, never an added row-encoding premise.

# The first machine configuration in the derived finite strip

Row encoding means actual north colors in the open interval and an
interior machine head. It asserts no transition or halting theorem.
The marked-word initialization theorem derives this encoding for the
actual machine after its first blank-tape step.

commits.subject: Bind operational color updates to actual transition signals and receiver targets

modules.module_doc:
# Actual decimal transitions and literal Wang-table actions

The input index is `2*q+b`. The existing complete decoder/cache theorem
binds its literal action to the actual machine transition. Target bounds
come from the already proved actual direction-specific target sets, so
the target215 is exactly the optional halt state and not an out-of-range
operating state. No decimal numeral or full table is reevaluated here.

Actual input indexing, target-state and action-color binding checks.
The only concrete target computation is over the proved small action cache.

# Actual operational step in vertical colors

A live-state action writes at the old head and moves exactly one cell.
The destination therefore reads its old tape bit. Its new head color uses
the action's actual optional next state, including entry into halt.
No tile-row, run-calibration, or consistency premise is used.

Direction, write/erase, entering-halt, and unchanged-cell checks for
the actual operational three-way color formula.

# Local signal matching in the actual 942-tile language

Plain-input neighbors cannot match a nonzero signal to one another. A
transition's outgoing signal forces the appropriate receive tile with exactly
its actual target, including target 215. No whole-row or run assumption is used.
Exact direction, target, halt reception, and retained finish checks.

commits.subject: Prove strict Wang-strip head containment and sharp actual trace bounds

modules.module_doc:
# Explicit finite bounds for actual blank machine traces

The bounds follow directly from the repository's write-before-move operational
semantics. They include entry into halt and stationary halted steps. No tape
normalization, tiling, or run-calibration hypothesis is used.
Sharp endpoint, halt-entry, stationary-halt, and unnormalized-tape checks.

# The actual stepped head remains strictly inside the strip

A transition's active rail has color at least6. The right wall's west
color is at most4 and the left wall's east color is at most2. Actual
horizontal matching therefore prevents either move from entering a wall.
The proof uses no absence-of-finish or time-matching premise.

The next-head result uses only allowedness, horizontal matching,
the existing strip and live row encoding; no time or no-finish premise.

commits.subject: Prove actual Wang row evolution and construct its reverse step row

modules.module_doc:
# Actual machine steps in the derived Wang strip

The operating head writes, its adjacent receiver gets the exact next head
color, and every other interior tile passes its old bit. Signals cannot
appear between two plain inputs or enter from a seam wall. Absence of a
finish row is derived from the operating head, never supplied as a premise.

Focused composition checks for actual row evolution, including entry
into halt, the original destination bit, the marked plane and clock1.

# Construct the exact Wang row of an actual operating machine step

The old head uses its literal transition tile, the moved head uses the receive
tile for its actual target and old tape bit, and every other cell passes its bit.
Entry into halt is included. This constructs a whole-integer matching row; it
assumes no row/step equivalence or finite-rectangle calibration.
Whole-row, actual first action, left move, and halt-entry reception checks.
